title: The Adventure of the Speckled Band

teacherSummary.text: Helen Stoner fears for her life: her twin sister Julia died two years before, crying 'It was the band! The speckled band!' Now her violent stepfather, Dr. Grimesby Roylott, has moved her into Julia's room. Holmes and Watson notice a dummy bell-rope, a ventilator and a bed bolted to the floor. They wait in the dark; Holmes strikes at a swamp adder sent through the ventilator. The snake turns and kills Roylott, who had wanted the girls' inheritance.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “It is fear, Mr. Holmes. It is terror” slowly and put it in my own words: Helen tells Holmes that she is not shivering from cold but from fear and terror. Next, craft. I notice the repeated frame "It is fear... It is terror," which climbs from a milder word to a stronger one. The strongest word is “terror”: it names a fear that has taken over completely, worse than ordinary fear. Then, effect. What does Helen Stoner's answer tell Holmes about why she has come? My answer: Helen Stoner's answer that it is not cold that makes her shiver but fear tells Holmes she has come because her life is in danger; her body is reacting to a real threat, not imagination.
